question.text: Which option-pricing model do Indian exchanges use for the theoretical pricing of exchange-traded currency options?

answer.text: A simple cost-of-carry model with no volatility input
A historical-average-premium model based on the last 30 trading days
No theoretical pricing model is used — premiums are set purely by order matching

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Currency Derivatives workbook describes that Indian exchanges use the Black-Scholes options pricing model for the theoretical pricing of exchange-traded currency options. Black-Scholes takes spot, strike, time to expiry, interest rate, and volatility as inputs and produces a fair value used as a reference price. The Trap: A bare cost-of-carry model omits volatility, which is essential for option pricing. Premiums are not set by a 30-day historical average, and the exchange's theoretical price is computed by a model — not absent altogether. Note: The NISM Series I (Currency Derivatives) workbook page reviewed states that Indian exchanges use the Black-Scholes model for theoretical pricing of exchange-traded currency options. A specific Garman-Kohlhagen domestic/foreign two-interest-rate currency-option formula was not located in the workbook pages reviewed, so this item is reframed to the source-supported Black-Scholes statement.
